data.title: Acyclovir
data.summary: IV Antivirals — Anti-herpes · Synthetic acyclic guanosine (nucleoside) analogue
data.body:
_Oral · IV Antivirals — Anti-herpes_

**Class:** Synthetic acyclic guanosine (nucleoside) analogue

## Mechanism of action
- Phosphorylated first by viral thymidine kinase (so it is activated only in infected cells), then by host kinases to acyclovir triphosphate
- Acyclovir triphosphate competitively inhibits viral DNA polymerase and is incorporated into viral DNA → chain termination
- Active against HSV-1 and HSV-2 (most), VZV (needs higher doses); weak against EBV and CMV

## Pharmacokinetics
- Oral bioavailability only 15–30% → frequent dosing
- Half-life about 2.5–3 h; excreted unchanged by the kidneys (glomerular filtration and tubular secretion)
- Reduce dose in renal impairment

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Genital herpes: first episode, recurrences, suppression
- Herpes labialis (severe or frequent), eczema herpeticum, herpetic whitlow
- Herpes zoster (start within 72 h) and varicella in adolescents/adults or complicated cases
- HSV-associated recurrent erythema multiforme (suppression)
- Severe or disseminated infection, encephalitis, neonatal herpes (IV)

## Dose & formulations
- First-episode genital herpes: 400 mg three times daily (or 200 mg five times daily) × 7–10 days
- Recurrent genital herpes: 400 mg three times daily × 5 days, or 800 mg twice daily × 5 days, or 800 mg three times daily × 2 days
- Suppression: 400 mg twice daily
- Herpes zoster: 800 mg five times daily × 7 days
- Varicella: 20 mg/kg (max 800 mg) four times daily × 5 days
- Severe/disseminated HSV or VZV: 10 mg/kg IV every 8 h (neonatal herpes 20 mg/kg every 8 h)

## Adverse effects
- Oral: nausea, diarrhoea, headache (generally very safe)
- IV: crystalline nephropathy (keep well hydrated, infuse slowly), phlebitis at the drip site
- Neurotoxicity (confusion, tremor, hallucinations) in elderly or renally impaired patients

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity to acyclovir or valacyclovir
- Dose reduction (not contraindication) in renal impairment

## Drug interactions
- Probenecid and cimetidine reduce renal clearance
- Mycophenolate: both drugs' levels rise
- Other nephrotoxic drugs (with IV acyclovir)

## Monitoring
- Renal function with IV use or in the elderly

## Pregnancy & lactation
Considered safe (old FDA category B); used for first-episode and late-pregnancy suppression of genital herpes. Compatible with breastfeeding.

## Viva points
- Needs viral thymidine kinase for activation → selective for infected cells
- Resistance (TK-deficient mutants) occurs in the immunocompromised → foscarnet or cidofovir
- Zoster needs about 4 times the HSV dose
- Hydrate patients on IV acyclovir

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.11 (Systemic antiviral agents); Khopkar ch.3. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
